hypothesis: Training with on-policy ORPO (using the model's own drafts as rejected examples against gold chosen) should push coverage higher than the SFT baseline, because the model is penalised for the specific gaps it actually produces rather than generic negatives.
technique: A single greedy on-device call using a LoRA adapter fine-tuned with on-policy ORPO for 1 epoch (chosen = gold questions, rejected = the model's own prior drafts), replacing the SFT baseline adapter.
result: Scored 0.396 on the full-30 gate (2 wins / 4 ties / 23 losses vs Sonnet); rubric showed atomicity=4, specificity=3, coverage=3, naturalness=4, non-redundancy=3, and specPass=100%. Coverage did not improve over the SFT baseline — the on-policy preference signal failed to move the coverage dimension — so the experiment was discarded.

stages.text: On-policy ORPO adapter, single greedy draft
